Numa Triples ARR, Raises $45M Series C to Run the Entire Dealership
News provided by
Numa
Nov 16, 2026, 10:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Led by Blue Cloud Ventures, the round brings total funding to $96 million, with more than 1,500 dealerships across the U.S. and Canada already running on Numa's AI Operating System
SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Numa , the AI Operating System for dealerships, today announced a $45 million Series C led by Blue Cloud Ventures, with participation from Threshold Ventures, Costanoa, Touring Capital, Gradient Ventures and Tokio Marine Future Fund. The round brings Numa's total funding to $96 million. It caps a year in which Numa tripled in size, tripled its annual recurring revenue and became the AI system GM, FordDirect, BMW and Stellantis each put in front of their dealerships.
Numa has already won the hardest part of the dealership: the customer conversation. The system has handled more than 1 billion calls, texts and chats and booked more than 4 million appointments. Dealerships that run on Numa stay and grow with it. Net revenue retention has risen over the past year, and more dealerships are moving to longer agreements.
For decades, dealership software was built one task at a time. Each system kept its own record of what happened, and none of them acted on what the customer just said. The first wave of AI did not change that. It answered faster, then handed the work back to people to chase by hand.
Numa does not hand the work back. It knows not just who the customer is but what they need, and it acts on it: booking the visit, finding the right car, routing the call or flagging the customer about to leave.
"In two years, every general manager will have an AI COO," said Tasso Roumeliotis, founder and CEO of Numa. "At more than 1,500 dealerships, they already do, and it is Numa. It knows every conversation in the store, sees what needs attention and runs the work that follows. That is not another dashboard or another point tool. It is an operating system. The DMS was built to record the dealership. It was never built to run it. Numa was, and this round puts more engineers to accelerate it."
"What is unique about Numa is that the company understands the DNA and culture of a dealership and seamlessly AI-enables the workflow while empowering all constituents including the dealerships customers", added Mir Arif, Managing Partner of Blue Cloud Ventures. "Numa is not prescriptive but rather deeply understands the objectives of the BDC representative, the salesperson, the service technician, the parts specialist and the sales manager and significantly enhances their productivity."
"As an insurer, we view dealerships as a critical part of the ecosystem that supports customers throughout their vehicle ownership journey," said Mitsutoshi Shizuru, Managing Executive Officer of Tokio Marine & Nichido Fire Insurance Co., Ltd, "Numa is using AI to make this important customer touchpoint faster, more efficient, and more seamless. We believe Numa's technology has the potential to revolutionize the relationship between dealerships and their customers and help shape the next generation of mobility customer experiences in the U.S. and beyond."
This year, Numa took its system across the whole store.

articles.snippet:
TKTMJ has received a $42.4 million Army contract for construction and site work in Metairie, Louisiana. The Natchitoches, Louisiana-based small business will provide construction access to the work site, demolition, clearing and grubbing, excavation, embankment placement, geotextile and stone installation, and turf establishment and maintenance.
The post TKTMJ Wins $42.4 Million Army Corps Construction Contract In Louisiana appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
TKTMJ Wins $42.4 Million Army Corps Construction Contract In Louisiana
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 10:46 AM
TKTMJ Wins $42.4 Million Army Corps Construction Contract In Louisiana
TKTMJ has received a $42.4 million Army contract for construction and site work in Metairie, Louisiana. The Natchitoches, Louisiana-based small business will provide construction access to the work site, demolition, clearing and grubbing, excavation, embankment placement, geotextile and stone installation, and turf establishment and maintenance.
The firm-fixed-price contract was competitively procured through an internet solicitation. The government received four bids.
Work will be performed in Metairie and is expected to be completed by November 15, 2027. The contract is identified as W912P8-27-C-A003.
The full $42.4 million contract amount was obligated when the award was made using fiscal 2027 civil expenses funding.
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers’ New Orleans District is the contracting activity. The district oversees flood-risk management, navigation, coastal restoration, environmental, and other civil works projects throughout southern Louisiana.
Although the announcement does not name the specific project, the listed activities indicate a substantial civil construction effort involving preparation, earthwork, ground reinforcement, stone placement, and final site stabilization.
Construction access work will allow personnel and equipment to reach the active site. Demolition, clearing, and grubbing will remove existing structures, vegetation, debris, and other obstructions before excavation begins.
Excavation and embankment placement will reshape the site in accordance with the project design. Geotextiles can separate, reinforce, filter, or stabilize soil layers, while stone is commonly used for drainage, erosion control, structural support, or surface protection.
Turf establishment and maintenance will stabilize completed areas and restore ground cover after major construction activity.
The firm-fixed-price structure establishes an agreed amount for the defined scope, placing much of the performance-cost risk on TKTMJ unless the government authorizes changes.
Because the Army Corps obligated the entire amount at award, the $42.4 million represents a funded contract rather than an ordering ceiling or value dependent on unexercised options.

NEW YORK, NY – WEBWIRE – Tuesday, November 10, 2026
Garage Founders: Alaz Sengul (CTO) and Martin Hunt (CEO)
Garage , the leading AI-powered marketplace for America�s essential equipment, today announced $41 million in Series B funding led by Invus Opportunities, along with Infinity Ventures, Initialized Capital, Y Combinator, Benchstrength, and FJ Labs. The round brings the company�s total capital raised to $60 million and will accelerate hiring and expansion into new heavy-duty verticals, including public works and sanitation.
The Problem: A Trillion-Dollar Heavy Duty Equipment Market Still Running Offline
Despite representing a $1 trillion market, the process of buying and selling heavy duty assets remains fragmented, opaque, and largely offline. Local governments and essential service providers still rely on labor intensive and archaic means to manage the procurement and disposition of their most essential assets. The broken system strips communities of critical capital and time that could otherwise be reinvested directly back into local communities nationwide.
�Garage is digitizing a massive, trillion-dollar secondary market that has been entirely overlooked by modern technology,� said Bryan Kim, Partner at Invus Opportunities. �Reaching $100 million in annual sales with zero logistics employees is a testament to the power of their AI-driven platform. Martin and his team have not only built a highly efficient marketplace, but they�ve fundamentally rewired how local governments and private operators procure essential heavy equipment across all 50 states.�
Garage�s Solution: AI-Powered Marketplace Connecting Every Community in America
Garage has built the first AI-powered marketplace specifically for transacting the heavy equipment that keeps America�s communities moving. By streamlining every step of the transaction, the platform connects local communities directly to a national market, transforming a complex, months-long process into a modern, transparent digital experience.
�Garage has been a game changer for us. We recently sold an almost 40 year old fire truck for nearly $40,000, an apparatus that traditionally may have brought little more than scrap value,� said Chief Rob Reardon, Duxbury Fire Department (MA). �Garage made the process simple and helped us recover real value that we would not have seen otherwise. Those funds were put towards the cost of future apparatus, ultimately saving our community money.�

articles.title: Garage Raises $41M for its AI-Powered Marketplace for Fire Trucks and Municipal Equipment
articles.snippet: The most Auburn, Massachusetts ever got for a retired fire department unit was about $10,000. Then it listed one on Garage and sold it for $120,000. The difference had little to do with the truck and everything to do with who could see it. A former firefighter and EMT is betting that gap runs through a market the company sizes at $1T, and Garage just raised $41M, bringing its total to $60M, to carry the model from fire trucks into garbage trucks and public works.
